newsitem.title: USA: Textron Inc Q3 industrial revenues surge.
newsitem.headline: Textron Inc Q3 industrial revenues surge.

text.p: Textron Inc said on Thursday acquisitions helped lift revenues at its industrial businesses by 60 percent to $518 million in the third quarter over the year-ago quarter.

The company said those acquisitions, which included the Elco fastening-systems group, made in late 1995 and the first half of this year lifted the earnings of its industrial unit by 47 percent to $53 million.
Share earnings were up 17 percent to $1.40, the company said in its third-quarter results report.
Revenues at Textron's aircraft unit of $610 million were flat with last year, while income increased five percent to $69 million.

The company said revenues and income at its Bell unit dropped because of lower sales of military helicopters to the U.S. government and lower revenues on its V-22 EMD contract. The drop was offset in part by higher commercial helicopter sales. Cessna's results increased, due to higher sales of business jets and utility turboprop aircraft.
As of September 30, total aircraft backlog was $3.3 billion, Textron said.
Drops in U.S. government orders also hurt Textron's systems and components units. Revenues dropped 17 percent to $229 million and income decreased four percent to $23 million.

Textron's automotive revenues rose five percent to $365 million and income was up eight percent to $28 million. A pickup in North American automotive production, particularly in light trucks at Chrysler Corp, boosted sales.
Finance unit revenues increased five percent to $526 million, while income rose two percent to $98 million.
